ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the left port is labeled as input V1(s), the right port is labeled as output V2(s), and the bottom is a common reference node wire. Between the upper end of the input and the upper end of the output, a capacitor labeled 100 μF is connected in series. From the upper output node downward to the common bottom node, there is a vertical branch: first through a 10 kΩ resistor, then through a 100 μF capacitor, the two being in series. The positive terminal of V2(s) is at the upper output node, and the negative terminal is at the bottom common node, so the output voltage is across the two ends of this right-side series RC branch. Then reason: According to the specified method, model the top 100 μF capacitor as a series impedance Z1 = 1/(sC). Model the resistor-capacitor series branch on the right side from the output node to the common bottom node as the load impedance Z2 = R + 1/(sC). The circuit is Z1 and Z2 in series, and V2(s) is taken across the two ends of Z2, so the voltage division relationship is V2(s)/V1(s) = Z2/(Z1 + Z2). Substitution gives V2(s)/V1(s) = [R + 1/(sC)] / [1/(sC) + R + 1/(sC)]. Multiplying both by sC gives (sRC + 1)/(sRC + 2). In the figure, R = 10 kΩ, C = 100 μF, so RC = 10000 × 100×10^-6 = 1. Therefore the transfer function simplifies to (s + 1)/(s + 2).
